title: Procurement Savings
summary: Reducing third-party spend through better sourcing, vendor consolidation, and contract discipline.
definition: Reducing third-party spend through better sourcing, vendor consolidation, and contract discipline.
whyItMatters: PE cares because the initiative can convert operating diagnosis into measurable EBITDA, cash flow, growth quality, management accountability, or exit multiple support.
commonProblems: Management has anecdotes but no clean baseline.
The company tracks activity but not value impact.
Owners are unclear and initiatives compete for attention.
diagnosticQuestions: Where is the value leakage visible in the P&L, balance sheet, or operating dashboard?
Which segments, sites, customers, SKUs, vendors, or teams drive the variance?
What can be changed in the first 30, 60, and 100 days without breaking the business?
process: Define the value hypothesis and KPI baseline.
Segment the business to isolate where the opportunity lives.
Prioritize quick wins, structural fixes, and longer-term capability builds.
Assign owners, cadence, and benefits tracking.
Report progress through the value creation dashboard.
ebitdaLogic: The lever improves enterprise value by increasing EBITDA, releasing cash, making growth more durable, or creating a better diligence story that buyers can underwrite.
caseExample: In a sponsor-backed company, the team builds a baseline, targets the highest-variance segments, launches a 100-day sprint, and uses weekly value tracking to separate real savings or growth from one-time noise.
hundredDayPlan: Days 1-30: baseline data, confirm opportunity, name executive owner.
Days 31-60: launch pilots, install dashboard, remove blockers.
Days 61-100: scale what works, lock cadence, quantify run-rate impact.
commonMistakes: Treating the playbook as a one-time project instead of a management system.
Counting theoretical benefits that never hit EBITDA or cash.
Skipping change management with the operating team.

articleSections.title: Procurement as a Value Creation Engine
body: In the middle-market private equity space, procurement is often an untapped reservoir of EBITDA expansion that can be unlocked rapidly within the first 12 months of ownership. Many portfolio companies suffer from fragmented spend, where decentralized purchasing decisions lead to a proliferation of vendors and a lack of volume-based leverage. We view procurement not just as a back-office function, but as a strategic lever to capture 'Operational Alpha' by professionalizing the supply chain and consolidating the external spend base.

Successful operating partners begin by conducting a 'Spend Cube' analysis to categorize every dollar of external expenditure by vendor, category, and business unit. This analysis, often supported by specialized tools like Coupa or SpendHQ, provides the visibility needed to identify 'maverick spend'—purchases made outside of negotiated contracts. By mandating that 80%+ of spend is 'under management,' we can typically drive a 5-10% reduction in total material and service costs without impacting operational quality.

The impact of procurement savings is magnified at exit because it represents 'pure' EBITDA margin expansion with high earnings quality. For a $300M revenue business with $150M in external spend, a 5% savings initiative adds $7.5M directly to the bottom line. At a 12x exit multiple, this seemingly technical operational improvement creates $90M in incremental enterprise value, delivering a massive return on the resources deployed to professionalize the procurement function.
articleSections.callout: Every dollar saved in procurement is a dollar added to EBITDA; it is the most direct path to margin expansion.

articleSections.title: Direct Spend: Strategic Sourcing and SKU Rationalization
body: For manufacturing and distribution assets, optimizing 'Direct Spend'—the raw materials and components that go into the product—is critical for protecting gross margins. We focus on 'Strategic Sourcing,' which involves renegotiating contracts with primary suppliers and introducing competitive bidding processes using e-sourcing platforms like Jaggaer or SAP Ariba. By consolidating volume with fewer, high-performance vendors, we can negotiate better unit pricing and more favorable payment terms (DPO).

Consider the math of 'SKU Rationalization' within a direct spend category. If a company uses 50 different types of fasteners across its product lines, consolidating down to 10 standard types can lead to a 15% reduction in material costs through sheer volume leverage. Furthermore, reducing the 'Tail-Spend'—the thousands of small, unmanaged purchases—by moving them to a 'Preferred Vendor' program can drive an additional 3-5% in annual savings with minimal management effort.

We also look for 'Should-Cost' modeling opportunities where we break down a supplier's cost structure to identify where we are overpaying for their overhead or profit. By utilizing engineering-led sourcing techniques, we can challenge supplier quotes with data-driven evidence of what a component 'should' cost in the current market. This level of granular negotiation transforms the supplier relationship from a purely transactional one into a strategic partnership focused on total value creation.

articleSections.title: Indirect Spend: The 'Low-Hanging Fruit'
body: Indirect spend categories—such as logistics, IT, telecom, office supplies, and professional services—are often the most fertile ground for 'Quick Win' savings. These categories are frequently unmanaged in founder-led businesses, with contracts that haven't been reviewed in years. We deploy 'Category Specialists' who use benchmarking data from firms like GEP or Accenture to identify where the portfolio company is paying significantly above the market rate for non-core services.

In the logistics category alone, we often find 10-20% savings by renegotiating carrier contracts and optimizing 'LTL' (Less-Than-Truckload) shipping routes using Transportation Management Systems (TMS) like MercuryGate. For a company with $20M in annual freight spend, a 15% improvement adds $3M to EBITDA. This $3M, when magnified by the exit multiple, represents $36M in enterprise value created within the first 100-200 days of the hold period.

We also focus on 'Demand Management'—reducing the consumption of indirect services rather than just the price. This involves implementing strict approval workflows in the ERP (e.g., NetSuite or Oracle) for discretionary spending and utilizing 'Virtual Cards' like Brex or Ramp to track and control employee expenses in real-time. By fostering a culture of 'Spend Discipline,' we ensure that the procurement savings are sustainable and don't 'creep' back into the P&L over time.

articleSections.title: Supply Chain Resilience and Working Capital
body: In the post-pandemic era, procurement is also about 'Supply Chain Resilience' and the optimization of working capital. We work with management to identify 'Single-Source' risks and develop 'Dual-Sourcing' strategies that ensure continuity of supply without significantly increasing costs. We use supply chain visibility tools like Resilinc or FourKites to monitor global disruptions and ensure our portfolio companies can pivot their sourcing strategies faster than their competitors.

Procurement also plays a lead role in improving the 'Cash Conversion Cycle' by negotiating longer payment terms with vendors. If we can move the average 'Days Payable Outstanding' (DPO) from 30 to 45 days for a company with $180M in annual spend, we release $7.5M in cash from the balance sheet. Because this cash can be used to pay down debt or fund acquisitions, it has a direct and positive impact on the internal rate of return (IRR) of the investment.

We also focus on 'Inventory Optimization' as part of the procurement workstream. By integrating procurement data with sales forecasts (S&OP) in tools like Anaplan or o9 Solutions, we can reduce the 'Safety Stock' levels and minimize the amount of working capital tied up in raw materials. This 'Just-in-Time' sourcing mentality ensures that we are only buying what we need to meet confirmed demand, further enhancing the liquidity of the portfolio company.

articleSections.title: Institutionalizing the Procurement Function
body: The ultimate goal of our procurement initiatives is to build a permanent 'Procurement Muscle' within the organization that continues to deliver value long after we exit. This involves hiring a dedicated Chief Procurement Officer (CPO) and implementing a modern 'Source-to-Pay' (S2P) technology stack that provides ongoing visibility and control. We ensure that procurement is a core business function with a seat at the leadership table, rather than just a sub-department of finance.

Mathematically, the 'Professionalization Premium' is a key driver of the exit multiple. A strategic buyer will pay significantly more for a company with a data-driven, automated procurement function than for one with manual, fragmented purchasing processes. We document the procurement savings as a repeatable process, showing the 'Pipeline' of future initiatives to prove to the next owner that there is still 'Operational Alpha' left to capture in the supply chain.

In the final 12 months of the hold, we focus on 'Vendor Consolidation' and the finalization of long-term contracts to provide 'Price Certainty' to the buyer. This minimizes the perceived risk of future cost increases and ensures a smooth transition during the due diligence process. By providing a clean, transparent, and optimized spend base, we position the portfolio company as an 'Institutional Grade' asset that is ready for its next phase of growth under a new owner.
